cohort_applicability_note: After full-text review of the FY2023 10-K (and confirming with the most recent pre-cutoff 10-Q filed 2024-08-09), FTAI Aviation Ltd. is a commercial aviation lessor + aerospace aftermarket business. There are ZERO mentions of Pentagon Program Elements, named DoD programs, named DoD customers, IDIQ ceilings, or program-of-record narratives. Engines named (CFM56-7B, CFM56-5B, V2500) are commercial-aviation engines, not LM2500 marine gas turbines (the cohort note hinted at military adjacency via LM2500/CFM56 modules, but the LM2500 marine line is GE/RTX, and the filing contains no LM2500 reference). The only 'military' string mentions in either filing are geopolitical-risk language about Russia/Ukraine. Entity-resolution lookups: FTAI does not appear in ticker_entity_resolution.json, ticker_pe_crosswalk.json, or by_entity.json. Direct M-source checks: pentagon_jbook.query_program_funding(contractor_name='FTAI Aviation')=NOT_FOUND; usaspending.query_dod_contracts(recipient_name='FTAI Aviation')=0 awards. This is a NULL case for the J-Book exposure-divergence pattern; the framework should NOT generate red flags merely because the cohort hypothesis was investigated. We extract a handful of business-narrative claims for control purposes and document the absence of J-Book-grounded claims.
